newsitem.title: GERMANY: Oil World sees tight 96/97 world oilseeds balance.
newsitem.headline: Oil World sees tight 96/97 world oilseeds balance.

text.p: Global oilseeds supplies in 1996/97 were pegged at 288.30 million tonnes, down 3.27 million tonnes from the previous season, the Oil World newsletter said.
While production was higher than in 95/96 at 257.11 million (255.22), carry-in stocks of 31.19 million tonnes on Oct 1, 1996, were sharply down from 36.35 million a year earlier.

Oil World forecast ending stocks on Oct 1, 1997, at 27.10 million tonnes, adding this would make it necessary to expand oilseeds plantings for the 97/98 season, given that demand for seeds, meals and oils was forecast to rise.
Soybean output in 96/97 was seen at 132.98 million tonnes compared with 124.27 million previously but carry-in stocks were only 22.07 million tonnes versus 29.08 million previously.
Supplies in 96/97 of nine oilseeds other than soybeans would be boosted by high opening stocks, Oil World said.
But production of rapeseed, sunseed, cotton seed and linseed were forecast lower, which more than offset supply additions from higher palmkernel, copra and groundnut crops.
Oil World cited reduced areas, yield losses and competition with lucrative grain crops for acreage for the declines.
World 96/97 rapeseed crops were estimated down 4.36 million tonnes at 30.12 million and sunseed off 1.52 million at 24.45.
